items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: one of my most successful early records was “Dear Mr. Cole” with Benny Green and Christian McBride. And we never worked together.

ctx.x: I thought it was wonderful that you had your trio on the record. And like people might say well yeah, well of course. But a lot of times people have ringers or whatever, and you have built in ringers.

Yeah I mean I made a record — one of my most successful early records was “Dear Mr. Cole” with Benny Green and Christian McBride. And we never worked together. And we had a great time making the record but I really have to say I’m really pleased that we were able to have the group and bring the group out, especially with Isaiah’s success so early, winning the American Pianist Award and being so popular at the moment and things like that. But he has expressed to me that he likes — wants to stay in the band as long…

That’s what you said pretty much 23 years ago when we met. I had asked you the question what are your goals in, I said, 15 years. But you said that, that you wanted to keep doing what you’re doing, do it better, be more organized, make some better bread.
